title: [feat]/ Support four independently controlled DJ decks
problem: Layered mixing needs four decks; DECKS is fixed at two and deck commands alias higher deck IDs. Serato four-deck availability depends on hardware.
acceptance: Provide four independent transport, cue, loop, gain and meter states
Keep a two-deck mode without silently remapping active deck IDs
Route and record all four decks with persistent deck identity
validation: Play four distinct test tones, operate each deck independently, then validate on a four-deck controller.

title: [feat]/ Add selectable DJ waveform and library layouts
problem: The fixed scratch/sampler/crate/sequencer stack cannot prioritize decks or a large library for different gig workflows.
acceptance: Offer horizontal, vertical/stacked and library-focused layouts
Preserve active-deck and controller focus across layout switches
Restore chosen layout and scale it to common laptop and external display sizes
validation: Inspect every layout at 1366x768, HiDPI and four-deck resolutions during playback.

title: [feat]/ Show aligned beatgrid, phase and phrase position on deck waveforms
problem: Existing frequency-colored waveforms lack editable beatgrid overlays and an explicit inter-deck phase view.
acceptance: Draw downbeats, beats and saved cue/loop markers against the audible playhead
Offer synchronized zoom and a phase-offset display between selected decks
Keep visual position aligned with output latency during scratching and tempo changes
validation: Compare rendered positions against captured click-track output and test long-track zoom during playback.

title: [feat]/ Add a dedicated track preparation and audition workflow
problem: Users can play without hardware, but preparing cues, grids and crates competes with the live two-deck layout; no separate preview player exists.
acceptance: Provide an independent preview player with level and seek controls
Allow cue, loop and grid preparation without replacing a performance deck
Provide keyboard navigation and an explicit preview output choice
validation: Prepare a set while two decks play and prove preview audio never leaks to the master.

title: [feat]/ Create and edit persistent per-track beatgrids
problem: A scalar BPM and zero-based sample position cannot identify musical downbeats reliably. The current Sample and DeckRt have no beatgrid model.
acceptance: Represent downbeat position and beat coordinates separately from BPM
Allow set, slip, stretch, reset and half/double-tempo correction with visible preview
Persist manual edits by track identity and protect them from automatic reanalysis
validation: Use tracks with pickups, leading silence and half/double tempo ambiguity; reload and compare cue alignment.

title: [feat]/ Support manually mapped tempo changes within a track
problem: Live drummers and tempo-changing edits need piecewise grids; one BPM cannot keep later beats aligned. Stable Serato supports manual beat warp markers.
acceptance: Allow multiple ordered tempo anchors without changing original audio
Use local beat-to-time conversion for cues, loops and synchronization
Provide insert/delete and continuity validation at tempo boundaries
validation: Test a ramping click track and a live-drum fixture through loops, seeks and synchronization.

title: [feat]/ Separate tempo matching from beat and bar synchronization
problem: DeckSync sets a tempo target, and DeckMatch already performs one-shot modulo-beat alignment while both decks play. Missing professional scope is downbeat-aware persistent grids, explicit leader management, and sustained tempo-only versus beat/bar synchronization modes.
acceptance: Expose tempo-only, beat-aligned and disengaged sync states
Choose a sync leader explicitly and define what happens when it stops or unloads
Preserve intentional phase offsets during jog manipulation and re-arm phase sync predictably
validation: Record paired click tracks through leader changes and variable-tempo boundaries; measure beat error.

title: [feat]/ Add safe pitch-fader pickup and temporary pitch bend
problem: Moving a physical pitch fader after sync or a deck-layer change must not cause a tempo jump; current controls apply values directly.
acceptance: Implement soft takeover with a visible pickup target for absolute faders
Offer momentary bend up/down that returns to the base rate on release
Show original BPM, effective BPM and chosen pitch range separately
validation: Replay fader crossings and layer changes, then verify on an absolute-fader controller.

title: [feat]/ Qualify DJ time stretching for transparent key lock across tempo ranges
problem: The existing granular key-lock implementation has a zero-crossing test, not a broad musical fidelity and latency qualification. Pitch n Time is an optional Serato expansion; its proprietary algorithm is not assumed available.
acceptance: Provide a documented real-time stretching implementation with an appropriate license
Define supported tempo ranges and scratch/key-lock transition behavior
Pass a disclosed vocal, transient, bass and full-mix listening corpus with measured latency and CPU bounds
validation: Blind listening plus rendered reference measurements at several rates; verify no callback deadline regressions.

title: [feat]/ Analyze musical key and display harmonic compatibility
problem: Library key is currently inferred from filenames, not audio; professional harmonic selection needs analyzed keys and editable confidence-aware metadata.
acceptance: Analyze key in the background and distinguish inferred, user and analyzed values
Display conventional and harmonic notation without overwriting user edits
Expose confidence/unknown and permit correction for ambiguous material
validation: Use an independently labeled musical corpus, publish error rates and verify persistence.

title: [feat]/ Add independent deck key shift and harmonic key sync
problem: There is no independent semitone control or key-matching operation. Serato benchmarks these through optional Pitch n Time DJ.
acceptance: Shift key without changing tempo and reset to original key
Offer an explicit target-key sync action with a visible semitone offset
Use a licensed implementation and disclose supported shift range
validation: Compare tuned fixtures and full-mix listening samples at fixed tempo, including transition artifacts.

title: [feat]/ Name, color and persist per-track hot cues
problem: Eight cue positions exist only in deck state; they lack names, custom colors and a persistent track association.
acceptance: Store cue positions, labels and colors in the track library
Show cues consistently in waveform, pad and list views
Keep cue edits when tracks are reloaded or moved and distinguish temporary cue state
validation: Set all eight cues, rename and recolor them, reload the app and relocate the source file.

title: [feat]/ Implement hold-to-audition and stutter behavior for temporary cues
problem: The existing DeckCue arm sets or returns a position with a single event; it has no press/release audition state.
acceptance: Model cue press/release separately from play-toggle
Audition while held from pause and return on release unless play is latched
Define equivalent mouse, keyboard and MIDI behavior
validation: Assert audio position and output through all cue/play press-order combinations, then test hardware.

title: [feat]/ Apply beatgrid quantization to deck cues and loop operations
problem: DeckLoopIn, DeckLoopOut and DeckReloop already snap to a zero-origin grid derived from a scalar BPM when quantization is enabled. Missing scope is persistent downbeat-aware and variable-tempo grids, cue quantization and selectable musical divisions.
acceptance: Offer deck quantize on/off and selectable beat division
Quantize cue creation/trigger and loop in/out/reloop using the current grid
Show pending actions and avoid quantizing free scratching unexpectedly
validation: Timestamp triggered audio against a click grid before/after tempo anchors and rapid retriggers.

title: [feat]/ Add named persistent loop banks for each track
problem: DeckRt keeps only one transient loop region; prepared loop banks cannot be recalled across loads.
acceptance: Save multiple named loop regions per track with stable slot IDs
Recall, activate, reorder and delete loops from UI and mapped pads
Persist loop metadata and restore active/armed state according to a documented load policy
validation: Create loops near start/end and tempo changes, reload, then trigger each slot via MIDI.

title: [feat]/ Add precise loop boundary editing and beat-based loop movement
problem: Loop in/out, halve/double and reloop exist, but there is no displayed boundary editor or beat-relative move operation.
acceptance: Allow fine boundary adjustment with waveform feedback
Move a loop by selectable beat increments while preserving musical duration
Expose safe fractional and multi-bar loop lengths with track-boundary handling
validation: Test repeated boundary edits and loop moves during playback using discontinuity and timing checks.

title: [feat]/ Add beat-jump transport and controller pad controls
problem: Seeking currently uses waveform fractions or jog deltas; DJs cannot jump a musical number of beats reliably.
acceptance: Jump forward/back by a selectable beat count
Preserve relative beat phase and define behavior inside an active loop
Provide pad/keyboard bindings with visible jump size
validation: Null-compare matched jump positions in constant and variable-tempo fixtures.

title: [feat]/ Add slip playback with configurable release timing
problem: Scratching and cue juggling currently alter the only playhead; there is no background timeline to resume.
acceptance: Maintain a shadow playhead during scratch, cue and temporary-loop actions
Return to its predicted position when the action releases
Offer immediate or quantized release and show the return position
validation: Exercise nested gestures across tempo changes and verify sample position on release.

title: [feat]/ Add reverse playback and momentary censor controls
problem: Deck commands have no persistent reverse or momentary reverse-with-return operation.
acceptance: Support reverse transport with defined boundary/loop behavior
Provide hold-to-censor that resumes the forward timeline on release
Make direction explicit in waveform, UI and controller feedback
validation: Test direction switches and censor-release timing without clicks on several audio formats.

title: [feat]/ Add instant doubles and deck transfer
problem: Loading the same file again resets deck state; scratch routines need a copy of the active transport position and settings.
acceptance: Copy a source deck to a target with coherent playhead, pitch, loop and key state
Provide a separate move operation that preserves audible continuity
Respect target-deck load protection and show source/target clearly
validation: Compare output phase before and after doubles/transfers while looping and key locked.

title: [feat]/ Protect audible DJ decks from accidental load and eject
problem: A successful DeckAudio assignment replaces audio immediately; no performance-aware load lock protects an on-air track.
acceptance: Offer explicit lock of playing/audible decks for mouse, keyboard, drop, MIDI and IPC loads
Provide a deliberate override that identifies the target and preserves the old track until ready
Keep controller display and queued-load status synchronized
validation: Attempt every load/eject entry point while decks are live; verify uninterrupted output and correct override.

title: [feat]/ Add configurable crossfader assignments, curves and scratch cut-in
problem: The app exposes a single fixed two-deck crossfader response; four-deck mixes and scratch setups need assign/thru and response choices.
acceptance: Assign each deck to left, right or thru
Offer blend and sharp-cut curves with explicit cut-in and reverse controls
Keep gain transitions click-free and expose controller-mappable settings
validation: Measure gain versus fader travel and exercise fast cuts with two- and four-deck fixtures.

title: [feat]/ Add configurable elapsed, remaining and end-of-track deck warnings
problem: The deck readout has a remaining-time helper but no configurable elapsed/remaining display or visible runout warning policy.
acceptance: Let each deck show elapsed or remaining time with a clear mode indicator
Warn before track end using a configurable lead time
Suppress misleading runout alarms inside valid repeating loops
validation: Test short, long, paused, looped and variable-rate tracks against captured playhead state.

title: [feat]/ Enable live deck stem separation without interrupting playback
problem: Current built-in drum/harmony samples are not source separation. Professional live remixing needs real audio stems with bounded processing cost.
acceptance: Reuse the shared separation service for vocal, drums, bass and musical-bed deck streams
Prioritize playback and show processing readiness before stem actions become active
Handle model failure or overload with a coherent full-mix fallback, never partial silence
validation: Run mixed-genre files on declared CPU/GPU hardware while recording callback deadlines and audible artifacts.

title: [feat]/ Add per-stem mute, solo and level controls on decks
problem: There are no deck stem controls or controller pad state for live acapella/instrumental mixing.
acceptance: Provide individual mute/solo/level and quick vocal/instrumental selection
Keep stem state visible in pad colors and waveform presentation
Persist a documented per-load reset policy and support MIDI mappings
validation: Audition all stem combinations with prepared and still-processing tracks through UI and hardware.

title: [feat]/ Prepare and manage cached stems before a performance
problem: There is no readiness queue or cache management for separation; a show cannot depend on last-second inference completing.
acceptance: Queue selected tracks/crates for background separation with progress and cancellation
Validate cached stems by source identity and model version
Show disk usage and remove only generated stem data when clearing the cache
validation: Prepare a crate, restart offline, alter a source file, and verify stale-cache detection plus uninterrupted playback.

title: [feat]/ Apply performance FX and rolls to selected stems
problem: The current effects paths process tracks or the scene mix, not isolated components of a deck.
acceptance: Assign FX/roll actions to one or more stems with visible routing
Offer tempo-related parameters and momentary/latching behavior
Preserve timing and the unaffected stems when routing changes
validation: Record per-stem reference outputs through rapid FX selection and roll release.

title: [feat]/ Split stems across linked deck mixer channels
problem: Independent vocal and instrumental mixing needs linked transports with separate channel processing; no linked-deck state exists. Hardware-dependent Serato Stem Split is the benchmark.
acceptance: Duplicate an analyzed track into linked vocal/instrumental deck roles
Share transport timing while allowing independent gain and FX
Provide a safe unlink/restore action without losing original full-track state
validation: Measure phase coherence through sync, cue and loop actions across four-deck routing.

title: [feat]/ Add stem-specific slip performance gestures
problem: Serato 4.0.10/T10 introduces stem slip interactions; Omatainer has neither isolated stem playheads nor slip state. Treat hardware behavior as model-specific.
acceptance: Allow a chosen stem to enter a temporary slip gesture while other stems continue
Rejoin coherently at the shadow playhead with explicit release timing
Expose supported gestures and state on screen and in controller profiles
validation: Perform cue/scratch/release routines against multitrack references and test each advertised controller separately.

title: [feat]/ Add deck performance-pad modes with per-deck selection
problem: The 16-pad sampler is not a deck pad-mode system; hot cue, loop and advanced performance modes need a consistent command surface.
acceptance: Provide per-deck pad modes and parameter controls with consistent slot identities
Switch modes without leaving held notes or transient actions active
Allow controller profiles to expose supported modes and show labels/colors
validation: Hold pads while switching modes and deck layers; verify all releases reach the original action.

title: [feat]/ Add momentary loop-roll pad performance
problem: Auto/manual deck loops exist, but held beat-division rolls do not return to an advancing timeline.
acceptance: Trigger selectable beat-division rolls while a pad is held
Restore the underlying playhead on release
Offer per-deck quantization and coherent overlapping-pad priority
validation: Capture impulse-grid audio through held/retriggered rolls and confirm release position.

title: [feat]/ Add moving and fixed-loop slicer pad modes
problem: There is no grid-sliced deck performance mode for rearranging phrases live. Serato availability depends on hardware.
acceptance: Divide a selected beat domain into pad-addressable slices
Offer moving-domain and repeating-domain behavior
Provide quantized slice triggering and clear visual domain boundaries
validation: Run a numbered transient fixture through changing domain/quantize settings and hardware triggers.

title: [feat]/ Add scratch banks with instant return to the previous deck track
problem: Builtin stem loading does not provide user-configured scratch sample banks or restoration of the previous track state.
acceptance: Assign library tracks and cue start points to scratch-bank slots
Preload entries and recall start, loop and key-lock preferences
Return to the previous deck state deliberately after a scratch-bank routine
validation: Switch banks repeatedly while another deck plays and verify previous track restoration.

title: [feat]/ Add chromatic cue-point performance pads
problem: Sampler note transposition does not pitch deck cue points. Serato Pitch Play is tied to the optional Pitch n Time expansion.
acceptance: Choose a cue as the pad root and display semitone assignments
Offer selectable pitch ranges with explicit original-key reset
Keep deck tempo independent and release voices/actions correctly across modes
validation: Verify pitch using tonal fixtures and fast pad routines with cue selection changes.

title: [feat]/ Load user samples into persistent DJ sampler banks
problem: The existing sampler banks are generated in code and cannot be populated from arbitrary library audio.
acceptance: Assign local library samples to named reusable banks and slots
Expose per-slot gain, start/end and waveform audition
Persist file identity and report missing samples without silently substituting defaults
validation: Build a bank from mixed audio formats, restart, move a file and verify recovery.

title: [feat]/ Add trigger, hold and toggle sample playback modes
problem: Current sample-bank pads start one-shot playback, while instrument pads use note gating. Neither supplies explicit selectable trigger, hold and toggle semantics per DJ sample slot.
acceptance: Select trigger, gate or toggle behavior independently per slot
Offer repeat and cue-point start with predictable retrigger rules
Ensure emergency slot stop works across mouse, keyboard and controller input
validation: Test press/release/retrigger combinations and long held samples across bank changes.

title: [feat]/ Add beat-synced sampler playback and output assignments
problem: DJ sample loops need tempo matching and channel selection independent of the synthesizer-oriented sampler paths.
acceptance: Sync beat-tagged sample loops to the chosen performance clock
Assign sampler output to master, cue or a chosen deck/bus
Provide per-slot level/mute plus a dedicated sampler master
validation: Record loop phase through tempo changes and validate separate physical output routing.

title: [feat]/ Add assignable deck DJ-FX units with tempo controls
problem: Track/scene effect chains and global wet slots do not supply a coherent deck A/B FX assignment workflow.
acceptance: Create independently assignable units for decks, sampler and master
Support beat-synced and manual timing with visible wet/dry and bypass
Define pre/post-fader behavior and preserve tails when disengaged
validation: Impulse-test routing and tails, then operate mapped FX paddles during a mix.

title: [feat]/ Add selectable one-knob channel effects
problem: A deck filter knob exists, but no selectable channel-FX workflow does. Serato built-in Channel FX require supported hardware or Serato Play; expanded effects and advanced presets depend on the relevant entitlement.
acceptance: Select a documented set of one-knob channel effects with a neutral detent
Define consistent left/right behavior and safe switching of effect type
Expose assignment and current effect name to controller feedback
validation: Sweep controls, switch effect types at non-neutral settings, and check for gain jumps.

title: [feat]/ Save and share DJ effect presets and unit layouts
problem: Effects are ephemeral; performers cannot recall a named deck performance chain for a routine. Serato advanced presets are an expansion benchmark.
acceptance: Save names, order, routing and parameters of performance FX units
Recall atomically with an explicit tail/reset policy
Import/export a versioned preset without depending on proprietary Serato formats
validation: Round-trip presets and switch them during playback while checking routing and tails.

title: [feat]/ Add momentary and latched performance-pad FX
problem: The effect window is parameter-oriented and has no reusable deck pad-FX performance layer.
acceptance: Assign effect presets to pads with explicit hold or latch behavior
Allow beat-division and wet/depth parameter controls
Clear pending pad effects safely when changing modes or unloading a track
validation: Stress chorded pads, mode changes and track loads while recording effect state and audio.

title: [feat]/ Deliver a usable MIDI learn editor for performance controls
problem: README promises learning, but LearnCapture is ignored and there is no learn UI. This feature owns the complete capture-to-assignment implementation, editing and cancellation workflow.
acceptance: Select a mappable control, capture a physical message and preview its action
Show device/channel/message/target with replace, add and remove options
Exit or cancel learning without swallowing later performance input
validation: Perform assignment, conflict, cancel and device-disconnect flows with real MIDI and synthetic messages.

title: [feat]/ Persist, import and export MIDI mapping presets
problem: Compiled builtin tables cannot preserve user setup, device revisions or portable mappings.
acceptance: Save versioned per-device presets with explicit factory override layers
Load, duplicate, rename, export and restore defaults without code changes
Validate unknown actions and ambiguous mappings before activation
validation: Round-trip presets across machines and check factory fallback after malformed import.

title: [feat]/ Support configurable MIDI encoder encodings and high-resolution controls
problem: Fixing one reversed jog decoder will not cover differing signed encodings, pitch bend or paired high-resolution controls.
acceptance: Provide absolute and documented relative encoder interpretations per binding
Support paired high-resolution CC and pitch-bend values for appropriate actions
Allow inversion, range and sensitivity without global device assumptions
validation: Replay protocol fixtures and measure monotonic bidirectional response on representative encoders.

title: [feat]/ Add controller layers, modifiers and takeover policies
problem: A shared four-Boolean shift array cannot express independent device banks, multiple modifiers or safe fader pickup across deck layers.
acceptance: Scope modifiers to device and layer with explicit hold/toggle semantics
Allow the same physical control to target different decks or modes
Use pickup/range policies for absolute controls when a layer changes
validation: Test simultaneous devices and held modifiers across disconnects and mode switches.

title: [feat]/ Drive controller LEDs and meters from actual application state
problem: note_led is unused, and only the first output is opened; no connected controller receives authoritative state feedback.
acceptance: Route feedback to the matching device and its selected layer
Publish cue, loop, play, stem, pad-mode and meter state with bounded update rates
Resynchronize all feedback after reconnect or preset change
validation: Capture MIDI output and verify against UI state; inspect actual RGB pads and meters on supported hardware.

title: [feat]/ Add runtime controller discovery, enablement and reconnection
problem: MIDI is scanned only at startup. Beyond correcting false connected labels, users need attach/detach and reassignment without restarting a set.
acceptance: Detect arrival/removal and show actual connection/error state
Enable devices and choose presets/output pairings at runtime
Reconnect without stuck controls, duplicate input connections or unintended transport changes
validation: Unplug/replug two controllers under playback repeatedly, including permission and busy-port failures.

title: [feat]/ Follow external MIDI clock with transport and loss handling
problem: The parser fix alone does not estimate tempo/phase, select a master or handle external transport. This is a hybrid-performance requirement, not a claim that Serato offers arbitrary clock input.
acceptance: Follow a selected clock source using timestamps and stable tempo/phase estimation
Handle start, continue, stop and supported song-position messages coherently
Expose loss/jitter status and a chosen freewheel/stop policy without oscillating tempo
validation: Use captured and hardware clock sources with jitter, dropped pulses, tempo changes and disconnects.

title: [feat]/ Transmit stable MIDI clock and transport to external instruments
problem: Unused output helpers do not schedule musical timing or route clocks. This fulfills the repository claim and hybrid-set needs beyond Serato core comparison.
acceptance: Schedule clock and start/continue/stop against the audio transport rather than UI repaint
Choose output ports independently and avoid sending clock to every device
Provide configurable timing compensation and visible sync status
validation: Capture output timing at several tempos under UI/decode load and synchronize a physical drum machine.

title: [feat]/ Publish hardware profiles backed by end-to-end compatibility evidence
problem: Current family-name matches and a label-selection test do not establish a working controller. Broad Pioneer/Numark/Akai promises need per-model evidence.
acceptance: Version profiles by model, protocol and firmware where necessary
Publish tested transport, mixer, pads, jog, feedback and audio functions separately
Mark unknown Linux driver/protocol support as unverified rather than inheriting Serato compatibility
validation: Run recorded message fixtures plus physical-device end-to-end qualification for every advertised model.

title: [feat]/ Support explicitly qualified HID DJ media players
problem: Only midir MIDI input/output exists; CDJ-style HID deck assignment, browsing and displays are not implemented. Serato support is hardware-dependent.
acceptance: Implement a documented or legitimately licensed HID profile for at least one selected player
Offer deck assignment and library/transport controls without a control-tone path
Report unsupported firmware/devices clearly and avoid claims of universal CDJ support
validation: Requires the exact media-player hardware and firmware; verify reconnect, browsing and two-player operation.

title: [feat]/ Implement verified motorized platter control and calibration
problem: A controller name and jog binding do not provide motor drive, absolute rotation tracking or touch calibration for NS7/RANE-style performance.
acceptance: Define safe motor start/stop and touch/release behavior per supported model
Track high-resolution position with configurable platter speed and calibration
Stop motors safely on device loss and reject unsupported protocols
validation: Requires physical motorized hardware and measured rotation-to-audio response; simulator coverage alone is insufficient.

title: [feat]/ Publish library and deck information to supported controller screens
problem: Omatainer has no hardware display protocol or artwork/waveform transport. This is model-specific functionality, not generic MIDI support.
acceptance: Provide selected track, playing title, time and deck assignment on a qualified device
Send cue/grid/waveform/artwork data only where the protocol supports it
Bound bandwidth and refresh stale display content after load/reconnect
validation: Inspect exact supported hardware while rapidly browsing and loading; measure that feedback does not delay input.

title: [feat]/ Add optional digital-vinyl control using a supported control-signal format
problem: No audio input or control-tone decoder exists. Serato DVS is optional/hardware-dependent; NoiseMap licensing and Linux compatibility must not be assumed.
acceptance: Select a legally usable control-signal format and document compatibility
Decode speed/direction and available position into independent deck transport
Provide internal, relative and supported absolute modes with safe fallback on signal loss
validation: Requires real turntables/media players, compatible input hardware and test vinyl/CD; compare tracking under scratches and worn signal.

title: [feat]/ Add DVS signal calibration and diagnostics
problem: A usable control-tone path needs channel calibration and signal-quality feedback, which the present app lacks.
acceptance: Display stereo scope/quality, input levels and channel polarity diagnostics
Guide sensitivity calibration without ever routing control tone to master
Identify weak/noisy/missing signal and show the chosen fallback state
validation: Test phono/line sources, reversed channels, hum, dropout and damaged control media on real hardware.

title: [feat]/ Support safe DJ handover on qualified dual-computer hardware
problem: Generic device recovery is not a booth handover workflow; current startup owns one default device with no per-channel ownership view.
acceptance: Show channel/deck ownership and hardware-supported USB source selection
Allow an inactive channel to be prepared and handed over without replacing the audible one
Document a verified manual fallback where automatic switching is unavailable
validation: Requires two computers and a dual-USB mixer/controller; record continuous master audio throughout changeover.

title: [feat]/ Provide isolated cue/master headphone mixing and split cue
problem: The render loop collects PFL material in cue_l/cue_r, then replaces the sole stereo program pair with a cue_mix blend at lines 732–738. There is no separate headphone bus, so changing monitoring affects program output. This issue owns both correcting that isolation failure and delivering usable cue/master and split-cue monitoring.
acceptance: Keep the program pair independent of PFL/cue_mix, and route cue to a distinct chosen output pair with independent level and cue/master blend
Support multiple deck PFL choices and optional split-cue monitoring
Provide an explicit test-tone/routing check and never enable headphone material on master implicitly
validation: Requires multichannel hardware: capture master and headphone outputs simultaneously during cue selection.

title: [feat]/ Add a separately controlled booth monitor bus
problem: There is only a common master/cue mix; booth monitoring needs independent level and optional microphone exclusion.
acceptance: Expose a separate booth output assignment and gain
Allow preselected microphone inclusion/exclusion independent of master
Keep booth mute/level changes from affecting program or recording outputs
validation: Capture booth, master and recording buses independently on a multichannel interface.

title: [feat]/ Add live microphone and auxiliary DJ input channels
problem: The audio backend creates output only; mobile/open-format DJ sets need controlled mic and external-source inputs.
acceptance: Add selectable mic/aux inputs with gain, mute, meters and optional tone controls
Offer intentional talkover ducking with attack/release and a manual override
Choose inclusion independently for master, booth and recording
validation: Test a microphone and line source through multichannel capture, including feedback-prevention routing.

title: [feat]/ Add deck-isolated output mode for external mixers
problem: One interleaved mix cannot feed a club mixer with independent software decks while retaining correct status and recording behavior.
acceptance: Assign each deck to an independent hardware output pair
Bypass internal channel/crossfader processing according to an explicit external mode
Show which levels are software-controlled and accept an external mix return for recording
validation: Requires a multichannel interface/external mixer; verify channel isolation and the captured mix return.

title: [feat]/ Create a persistent DJ library with stable track identity
problem: App.library is rebuilt in memory from Music directories; cues, grids, analysis and set preparation need a durable DJ library separate from DAW projects.
acceptance: Assign stable track identities and persist paths, metadata and DJ analysis in a versioned store
Keep local, removable and provider track namespaces distinct
Handle interrupted writes and schema migration without losing prepared track data
validation: Import a mixed library, restart, migrate schema and interrupt updates; verify every identity and associated preparation data.

title: [feat]/ Import arbitrary folders, files and removable music libraries
problem: Scanning only ~/Music and ~/music to depth six omits common external-drive and custom-folder workflows. This adds product scope beyond moving the scan off the UI thread.
acceptance: Let users add/remove watched roots and import files/folders explicitly
Show progress and skipped-file reasons while preserving active playback
Track removable-volume identity and distinguish temporarily offline from deleted files
validation: Import nested files on an external drive, unplug/reconnect it, and verify no duplicate records or deck interruption.

title: [feat]/ Read and edit real audio metadata instead of filename guesses
problem: Artist/title/BPM/key are parsed from filenames and user edits cannot be persisted to tags or a sidecar.
acceptance: Read supported format tags while keeping filename fallbacks explicit
Edit key library fields singly or in a reviewed batch
Write tags safely where supported and retain sidecar values for read-only media
validation: Round-trip Unicode tags across MP3, FLAC, WAV/AIFF and read-only sources with original audio intact.

title: [feat]/ Add track ratings, colors and performance annotations
problem: LibItem lacks ratings, track color, grouping and notes needed to organize energy, clean edits and requests.
acceptance: Store ratings, color and freeform tags/notes per stable track
Expose these fields in search, columns and smart-crate rules
Support batch edits without changing audio files unless explicitly chosen
validation: Tag a large crate, restart and verify filtering plus metadata export.

title: [feat]/ Make library columns, sorting and view density configurable
problem: The crate draws six fixed-width columns with a hardcoded sort; professional browsing needs selectable metadata and stable multi-column ordering.
acceptance: Show/hide, reorder and resize library columns
Support primary/secondary sort and explicit manual crate order
Save column layouts and support compact and artwork-oriented views
validation: Check stable sort and selection with equal values, Unicode names and large result sets.

title: [feat]/ Add field-aware search and filtering across the music library
problem: Current filtering is only a lowercased title/artist substring; BPM, key, rating and exact criteria cannot be combined.
acceptance: Search across selected metadata fields with explicit query/filter semantics
Combine numeric ranges, key, tags and played/unplayed conditions
Switch between current crate and all-library search while preserving navigation context
validation: Run a documented query corpus against a 100k-track synthetic catalog and validate result correctness and latency.

title: [feat]/ Add named ordered crates and nested playlist organization
problem: The single scan result called crate has no saved user collections, membership or manual ordering.
acceptance: Create, rename and delete ordered crates with many-to-many track membership
Nest crates and move tracks without moving source audio
Preserve manual order and stable membership through refresh and relocation
validation: Build nested crates with overlapping tracks, reorder them, restart and verify no audio-file changes.

title: [feat]/ Add automatically maintained smart crates
problem: No rule-based collections exist for key/BPM/genre/rating/date/playcount filtering.
acceptance: Define typed all/any rules over supported track fields
Update membership incrementally as metadata or analysis changes
Preview rule results and retain an explicit manual refresh option
validation: Validate a rules matrix and measure updates in a large library without blocking playback.

title: [feat]/ Add crate favorites, search and membership discovery
problem: Large organized libraries need fast crate access and a way to find every collection containing a selected track; no crate navigation exists.
acceptance: Pin favorite crates and search their names separately from tracks
Reveal which crates contain the selected track
Preserve selected track and scroll location when returning from results
validation: Navigate thousands of nested crates with keyboard and controller; verify context restoration.

title: [feat]/ Add a reorderable prepare queue for upcoming tracks
problem: The current single selection is not a holding area for requests and planned transitions.
acceptance: Add tracks/crates to an ordered prepare queue from browser and hardware
Choose remove-on-play versus retain behavior without conflating load with audible play
Save the queue as a reusable crate and restore it explicitly
validation: Queue requests while playing, reorder, preview, reject and load tracks, then verify policy and saved crate.

title: [feat]/ Record actual DJ performance history with session boundaries
problem: last_play is set at load time and exists only in memory; it cannot distinguish auditioned tracks from a performed set.
acceptance: Record session start/end, deck, actual audible play duration and track identity
Support played/unplayed marking and manual external-track entries
Keep history across restarts and permit export without exposing local paths unintentionally
validation: Load silent/cued tracks and crossfade audible ones; compare the history to multichannel audio capture.

title: [feat]/ Export and optionally publish performed setlists
problem: There is no performance-session export or opt-in now-playing feed. Serato History and Playlists are the comparison; standard CSV/text/playlist interoperability is proposed Omatainer scope, and Serato hosting is not assumed reusable.
acceptance: Export selected sessions as documented text/CSV and playlist references
Offer an optional now-playing endpoint with explicit enable/disable and redaction settings
Keep network errors and slow consumers off the audio path
validation: Verify exports against session data and exercise offline/reconnect conditions with a test consumer.

title: [feat]/ Add persistent background track analysis with selective reanalysis
problem: Decoding estimates BPM only when loaded and the scan does not prepare tracks; no analysis queue or preserved result lifecycle exists.
acceptance: Analyze selected tracks/crates off the real-time and UI paths with progress/cancel
Persist BPM, duration, waveform and optional key results by source/version
Offer selective reanalysis while preserving locked manual preparation
validation: Analyze mixed-format long tracks under active playback, cancel/restart and verify cached results.

title: [feat]/ Protect prepared beatgrids and metadata from bulk reanalysis
problem: Manual preparation needs explicit locking and provenance; current values have no authoritative source or locked state.
acceptance: Provide per-track grid/BPM/metadata locks with visible status
Show a preview of fields that an analysis or tag refresh will replace
Honor read-only files while allowing sidecar preparation
validation: Lock a prepared crate, run all analysis/import paths, and prove cue/grid/manual fields remain intact.

title: [feat]/ Analyze and recall safe per-track gain adjustment
problem: All decks initialize to the same gain; there is no loudness analysis or reviewed per-track auto-gain recall.
acceptance: Analyze a documented loudness/reference metric and store recommended gain
Enable auto gain with explicit target and headroom limits
Keep a user override and distinguish analyzed gain from current fader level
validation: Use quiet/loud/clipped fixtures, measure level/headroom after load and verify no unexpected gain jumps.

title: [feat]/ Expose missing, corrupt, unsupported and read-only track status
problem: The browser discovers by extension and hides walk errors; it cannot communicate track readiness before loading.
acceptance: Show actionable status for missing, corrupt, unreadable and unsupported media
Allow validation of selected crates without replacing live decks
Report errors per track and retain healthy files in partially failed imports
validation: Use truncated files, bad tags, permissions failures and absent drives; verify correct status and recovery.

title: [feat]/ Relocate missing music while preserving DJ preparation
problem: A path-only library loses prepared identity when folders are moved; there is no reconnect/relocation workflow.
acceptance: Locate missing tracks by selected replacement path or searched root
Validate identity and surface ambiguous matches before committing
Preserve cue/grid/crate/history associations across path changes
validation: Move and rename a music tree containing duplicate filenames and verify correct matches with rollback.

title: [feat]/ Manage music files and duplicates safely from the library
problem: There is no explicit copy/move/reveal/remove distinction or duplicate reconciliation for imported collections.
acceptance: Distinguish removing a library reference from deleting source audio
Copy/move selected files and update stable references after success
Detect likely duplicates and provide a reviewed merge preserving preparation metadata
validation: Simulate partial copy failures and duplicate filenames; prove no unselected file is deleted or overwritten.

title: [feat]/ Back up and move the complete DJ library with preparation data
problem: DAW project save will not preserve the independent music catalog, crates, cue points and histories.
acceptance: Export a consistent library snapshot with optional authorized local media collection
Restore into a new location with version checks and explicit merge/conflict handling
Verify source identities and preserve cues, grids, crates and history
validation: Restore on a clean user profile with different mount paths and verify a prepared set plays from the restored library.

title: [feat]/ Import standard playlists and existing local music-library exports
problem: There is no playlist import; users cannot bring a prepared local collection from music-app exports. Standard M3U interoperability is proposed Omatainer scope; the Serato 5.0 beta announcement describes M3U import returning, so this is not asserted as stable 4.0 parity.
acceptance: Import documented playlist formats with Unicode and relative paths
Offer local Apple Music/iTunes XML import when the export is available
Report unmapped/protected/provider-only entries without pretending audio was imported
validation: Use real exported fixtures on multiple platforms and verify order, path resolution and duplicate behavior.

title: [feat]/ Qualify sustained browsing and preparation on professional-size libraries
problem: Moving scanning off the UI thread and virtualizing rows fix current hot paths; professional scale also needs indexed queries, incremental updates and memory budgets.
acceptance: Define supported catalog sizes and measurable search/scroll/import latency budgets
Index metadata and apply incremental updates without rebuilding the whole view
Keep selection and playback stable through simultaneous analysis and filesystem changes
validation: Benchmark 10k/100k-track catalogs under a long-running mix, publishing hardware, memory and latency distributions.

title: [feat]/ Add deliberate continuous playback from an ordered crate
problem: Decks stop at track end and there is no explicit background-music/continuous-play mode. Serato Autoplay is a benchmark, not a claim of automatic beatmatched mixing.
acceptance: Play the next available item in the chosen ordered crate when a track finishes
Expose enable/disable, next-track preview and repeat policy
Skip/report unavailable tracks without disrupting another manually controlled deck
validation: Play a crate with missing and short files through end transitions, then disable autoplay during a transition.

title: [feat]/ Add licensed music-provider integration with explicit capability contracts
problem: All sources are local paths; supporting commercial streaming requires authorized APIs and per-provider capability rules rather than treating remote tracks as files.
acceptance: Define provider identity, authentication, search, playback and capability interfaces
Require supported authorization/licensing and platform feasibility before enabling a provider
Display offline/stems/recording/deck-count restrictions from current capabilities
validation: Use a contract test provider plus real authorized accounts before claiming a named integration; test token expiry and regional unavailability.

title: [feat]/ Integrate an authorized Beatport streaming workflow
problem: Beatport is a Serato benchmark provider; Omatainer has no account, catalog or playback adapter. Access terms and available plans must be verified before implementation.
acceptance: Support approved sign-in, catalog search and playlist navigation
Preserve provider track identity and permitted cue/grid metadata
Show subscription and track availability errors without interrupting local decks
validation: Requires an approved integration path and active test account; verify real search, load, playback and expiry.

title: [feat]/ Integrate Apple Music only through an authorized DJ playback path
problem: Apple Music streaming is distinct from local iTunes files; Serato currently restricts offline use, stems and recording for streamed tracks. Omatainer has no adapter.
acceptance: Verify an approved playback SDK/API and Linux feasibility before committing support
Implement account, catalog and playlist access with capability-aware controls
Keep local originals separate from cloud copies and retain metadata provenance
validation: Requires authorized service access on each advertised platform; test unavailable tracks, expired subscription and restrictions.

title: [feat]/ Integrate Spotify only if an authorized DJ service agreement is available
problem: Spotify is supported in Serato under service restrictions; a generic web API does not establish DJ audio playback rights or Linux support.
acceptance: Gate delivery on an approved DJ playback integration and supported platform path
Implement catalog/playlists/playback with explicit capability limits
Disable unsupported offline, stems and recording actions rather than bypassing restrictions
validation: Requires provider-approved end-to-end account and playback testing; otherwise remain explicitly blocked by external availability.

title: [feat]/ Integrate an authorized TIDAL DJ account and catalog
problem: TIDAL in Serato requires DJ entitlement and has provider-specific stems, quality and recording restrictions; Omatainer has no streaming implementation.
acceptance: Use an approved API to authenticate DJ entitlement and browse/search tracks
Select supported audio quality without hiding buffering/readiness state
Apply current stems/offline/recording capability limits to every playback path
validation: Validate with authorized entitled and non-entitled accounts, network loss and unavailable catalog entries.

title: [feat]/ Integrate authorized SoundCloud catalog and playlists
problem: Serato benchmarks SoundCloud Go+ playback, but tracks may be unavailable outside SoundCloud and require network access; no local provider adapter exists.
acceptance: Support approved sign-in, search and personal playlist browsing
Represent unavailable/external-playback-disabled tracks clearly
Persist permitted preparation metadata without assuming offline or recording permission
validation: Use an authorized test account with available, removed and app-playback-disabled tracks.

title: [feat]/ Manage provider-authorized offline lockers and readiness
problem: Offline streaming is provider- and plan-specific; local file loading is not a substitute for entitlement-aware cache handling.
acceptance: Allow download only when provider capabilities authorize offline playback
Show queued, ready, expired and unavailable status before a performance
Enforce cache lifetime/limits and delete revoked content without deleting user-owned media
validation: Prepare an entitled crate, disconnect the network and test playback, expiry, cache corruption and account logout.

title: [feat]/ Enforce streaming capabilities and protect playback during service failures
problem: Provider support must not imply blanket recording, stem extraction, offline use or unlimited decks; a policy layer and safe failure handling are absent.
acceptance: Check restrictions at deck load, stems, recording, export and offline-cache boundaries
Prebuffer where permitted and expose readiness without disrupting other decks
Handle token expiry, network loss, removed tracks and provider migration with honest status
validation: Use provider contract fixtures plus authorized live tests; verify local playback continues and no restricted derived files are created.

title: [feat]/ Record live DJ performances to reliable audio files
problem: The current Record command only toggles MIDI note capture; there is no master-mix recorder for a DJ set.
acceptance: Record the selected internal mix or external mix return with meters and destination controls
Write asynchronously with explicit format/bit-depth and safe long-file splitting
Finalize recoverable files on stop or failure and report disk-space/write errors before silent loss
validation: Record a multi-hour test mix, interrupt writes and decode-check recovered output; obey provider capabilities.

title: [feat]/ Expose a clean performance audio feed for OBS and broadcast tools
problem: No virtual/loopback output workflow exists for broadcasting a mix independently from monitoring. Serato uses a virtual audio path; direct streaming services are separate.
acceptance: Expose an opt-in program-only feed through supported platform audio routing
Keep cue and private preview material out of the feed
Provide level/latency checks and a documented OBS setup verified on Linux
validation: Capture through real OBS/PipeWire routing while cueing and changing devices; inspect recording for leaks/dropouts.

title: [feat]/ Link set recordings to performed-track and cue markers
problem: A recording file alone is hard to review or deliver; no relationship exists between audio capture and performance history. This is an Omatainer workflow proposal informed by separate Serato recording/history features.
acceptance: Associate recording sample offsets with track/deck history entries
Export an editable cue sheet or chapter/marker sidecar without modifying the audio master
Handle pauses/split recording files without losing time alignment
validation: Record known transitions with pauses and file splitting, then compare exported markers to decoded audio.

title: [feat]/ Record and replay nondestructive cue and censor routines
problem: There is no reusable deck edit/routine recording. Serato Flip is an optional expansion benchmark, not part of the baseline license assumption.
acceptance: Capture cue, censor and timing actions as an editable per-track routine
Replay with quantization, enable/disable and loop controls
Save multiple named variants without rewriting original audio
validation: Record a routine, reload the track and compare replayed action timing across tempo settings.

title: [feat]/ Add optional synchronized DJ video playback and external output
problem: No video pipeline exists. Serato Video is an optional expansion and platform-specific interop such as Syphon must not be promised on Linux.
acceptance: Decode video beside audio with a measured synchronization budget
Provide crossfader-linked transitions and a separate audience output window/feed
Isolate video decode/render overload so audio remains stable
validation: Test mixed codecs and external display changes with recorded audio/video synchronization and audio deadline monitoring.

title: [feat]/ Expose performance timing and mixer state for lighting systems
problem: There is no lighting interface. SoundSwitch integration is a separate third-party ecosystem; its private API and Linux availability are not assumed.
acceptance: Offer a documented transport/beat/deck/fader-state interface suitable for an authorized lighting adapter
Support a verified open timing path and explicit opt-in connection state
Keep lighting failures off the audio path and document unsupported third-party combinations
validation: Use an actual compatible lighting controller or separate supported host; verify beat, loop and fader response without claiming untested SoundSwitch support.

title: [feat]/ Detect changing-tempo beatgrids automatically as a preview-comparison feature
problem: Stable manual tempo anchors are a separate feature; Serato 5.0 public beta adds the newer automatic Lucid Beatgrids benchmark. Omatainer currently estimates one BPM.
acceptance: Analyze variable beat times with confidence and a choice of fixed/flexible grid policy
Preview changes and preserve locked/manual anchors unless explicitly replaced
Version analysis results so algorithm updates can be compared or reverted
validation: Evaluate a labeled live-drum/tempo-ramp corpus with documented beat/downbeat accuracy; beta benchmark is not claimed stable.

title: [feat]/ Mix approved streaming providers concurrently as a preview-comparison feature
problem: Serato 5.0 public beta advertises Open Streaming; stable 4.0 overview limits provider selection. Omatainer has no provider framework yet.
acceptance: Enable multiple authorized provider sessions without merging their identities or restrictions
Search provider catalogs with explicit source labels
Resolve concurrent deck loads and entitlement limits per provider without disrupting playback
validation: Requires approved live integrations for at least two providers and mixed outage/expiry tests; keep preview comparison labeled.

title: [feat]/ Trigger a saved loop from its associated cue marker
problem: Serato 5.0 public beta promotes Cue Loops; this is a preview benchmark beyond ordinary stable saved loops. Omatainer has separate transient cues and one loop.
acceptance: Associate a cue with an explicit loop length/region
Trigger cue and loop atomically with deck quantization
Display the association and allow a cue-only override
validation: Test cue-loop triggers across load/reload and tempo changes; label comparison as beta.
